text:
maria: Heads up — ap-southeast GPU nodes failing onboarding since ~04:12 UTC. Seen a bunch of KMS Deny errors and kernel join timeouts. Notifying here before paging.

chris: +1. Example from node-az3: `KMSAccessDenied: User arn:aws:sts::... assumed-role/node-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:.../key/abcd`

sanjay: We rolled the subnet-scoped KMS condition yesterday (`iam:Condition` limiting grants to subnet tags). Warm-pool nodes are getting placed into the maintenance subnet which doesn't match the new condition -> deny.

ops-bot: alert: keystore-proxy (keystore-proxy-72) returning 503 for /decrypt (count 42 in 5m).

jenna: If we open an exception we'll see a big bump in audit logs. Any quick estimate of ingestion/cost impact?

maria: Short answer: small but non-negligible. Rough estimate: ~10k extra audit events over 2h -> ~ $1.20 at current shipper rates. Priority is getting nodes online.

chris: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) Add the warm-pool subnet tag to the KMS condition allowlist. 2) Or create a temporary key alias with laxer condition and point keystore-proxy at it. Example command: `aws kms put-key-policy --key-id 1234abcd --policy file://tmp-allow-subnet.json`

chris: Quick health check commands I ran: `curl -sS -I https://keystore.internal.ap-southeast-1/health` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`; but proxy -> kms returns 403. Also ran: `aws sts get-caller-identity --output text` from failing node and it resolved IAM fine.

sanjay: Prefer not to create new key aliases unless necessary. Safer path is to update the condition to include `tag:node-pool=warm-pool` and rollback after the warm-pool drains.

alex: @maria @sanjay security note: we can approve an emergency 2-hour exception for the KMS condition if infra opens an incident ticket and documents rollback. Need explicit audit retention tag on the change and a postmortem.

maria: Opening incident now (INC-2026). I'll add the rollback plan: revert condition patch and run a canary joining sequence.

chris: Rolling a tiny policy patch to add the warm-pool tag to condition (will patch key policy in staging then production if green). Command I'm about to run: ```aws kms get-key-policy --key-id 1234abcd --policy-name default > current.json
# edit current.json to add \"StringEquals\": {\"aws:ResourceTag/node-pool\": \"warm-pool\"}
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id 1234abcd --policy-name default --policy file://current.json
```

deploy-bot: policy-change: kms-key/1234abcd updated by chris@infra — staging -> prod deploy started.

maria: Patch applied, starting node join watch. First 6 nodes in az3 started bootstrapping successfully. Will monitor for 30m.

jenna: Thanks. plz add cost tag `keystore:incident=1717171717` and I will run an audit-ingest query after. Also add a note about retention TTL so finance can estimate impact.

chris: Added tag and posted query to infra-dash. Early numbers look like ~7k events in the first 20m.

alex: Security sign-off for 2h exception granted. Reminder: full rollback within 2 hours, and include the change diff in the incident ticket.

maria: Will follow-up with a small ops postmortem and propose a longer-term fix: align warm-pool provisioning flow to annotate nodes with the correct tag before KMS grant evaluation.

jenna: Once PM cost estimate is in, we can decide whether to absorb or bill to project.

chris: Marking thread resolved for now. If any new denies show up I'll @channel. :thumbsup:
